families.name: 8-K item-level events: 5.02 officer/director departures, 4.01 auditor changes, 4.02 non-reliance restatements, 3.01 delisting notices

mechanism.class: behavioural underreaction to material news, amplified when filed after the close
literature: Denis & Denis (1995), Huson, Malatesta & Parrino (2004): CEO/officer turnover CAR approx -1% to -5%, larger for forced departures
Palmrose, Richardson & Scholz (2004): non-reliance restatements, mean 3-day CAR approx -9%
DeFond & Zhang (2014, survey): auditor-dismissal reactions -2% to -3% for problem-related changes, small/insignificant for administrative ones
Files, Swanson & Tse (2009): evidence of strategic timing/gaming of restatement filing dates

alternates: Sharadar EVENTS table (paid, $499/yr bundle, 8-K events from 1993, survivorship-free)
source.probe_evidence: data/event_scout/sec_edgar_submissions_aapl.json - AAPL 8-Ks show acceptanceDateTime to the second (e.g. 2026-04-20T21:29:51.000Z, items=5.02) and full item tags in every record

timing.timezone: UTC, ISO8601 with Z suffix; convert to America/New_York for market-open alignment
timing.next_tradable_execution: next regular session open (T+1 09:30 ET) for acceptances at/after 16:00 ET; same-day close-to-close otherwise

counts.events_per_year: 5.02 approx 1500-3000/yr; 4.01 approx 300-600/yr; 4.02 approx 100-300/yr (spiked >500 in 2021 SPAC-restatement wave), all across Russell-3000-sized filer universe
counts.history_available: EDGAR acceptance timestamps cover the full EDGAR era (1994+); universal full-text search from ~2001; Sharadar EVENTS from 1993

survivorship.event_side: unbiased - EDGAR captures every filer including later-delisted names
survivorship.price_side: needs a delisted-inclusive feed (Sharadar) for a full historical backtest; forward/recent work is fine on free feeds since target names are still listed at signal time

families.name: Overnight / marketed follow-on equity offerings (424B2/424B5 bought-deal pricing discount)

mechanism.class: compensated liquidity provision - underwriters/investors are paid a discount for bearing overnight placement risk
literature: Corwin (2003): SEO offer-price discount
Altinkilic & Hansen (2003): underwriting spreads and issue costs
Gao & Ritter (2010): accelerated vs. fully-marketed offerings, discount magnitude by deal type
Autore, Kovacs & Sisli (2009): shelf-registration discount dynamics

source.primary: SEC EDGAR 424B2/424B5 filings, cross-referenced with the same filer's 8-K Item 3.02/8.01
source.verified_in_session: indirectly, via the same confirmed EDGAR submissions API plumbing as family 1
source.caveat: ATM continuous-program draws are NOT individually timestamped in real time (only disclosed quarterly in the 10-Q); only discrete bought-deal 424B5 filings and ATM-program-LAUNCH filings are usable as sharp-timestamp events

timing.exact_field: acceptanceDateTime of the 424B filing, cross-checked against the pricing 8-K
timing.next_tradable_execution: next session open following an after-close pricing

counts.events_per_year: several hundred true overnight/marketed corporate equity follow-ons per year among Russell-3000-sized names; total 424B2/424B5 volume across all issuers (incl. debt) runs into the thousands/yr but most are not same-day-priced discrete equity events

clustering.profile: low-moderate - issuance clusters somewhat in risk-on windows, but dates are issuer-specific
clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: most of the raw count survives

survivorship.price_side: moderate risk - many issuers raise capital precisely because they are constrained, so some fail later; delisted-inclusive history wanted for a full multi-year backtest

families.quant_v7_contamination: GENUINELY NEW - no ATM/424B/overnight-offering work anywhere in research/; share_class.py tested dual-share-class ETF arbitrage, which is unrelated
families.implementation_realism: MEDIUM - needs same-day filing-to-pricing linkage (8-K + 424B cross-reference), more engineering than family 1 but the same free EDGAR plumbing

families.name: Buyback authorizations (first-time / re-up) and dividend initiations, cuts, omissions and specials (declaration date)

mechanism.class: managerial signalling - payout decisions convey private information not yet in price
literature: Vermaelen (1981); Ikenberry, Lakonishok & Vermaelen (1995): buyback announcement CAR approx +2% to +3%, plus a long-run drift finding that is now 30 years old and well known
Michaely, Thaler & Womack (1995): dividend initiations +3.4%, omissions -7%
Bernartzi, Michaely & Thaler (1997): dividend-change signalling

timing.next_tradable_execution: next session open/close depending on before/after-hours filing

counts.events_per_year: buyback authorizations approx 800-1200/yr among Russell 3000; dividend initiations approx 50-150/yr; cuts/omissions approx 100-300/yr (counter-cyclical); specials approx 200-400/yr; routine increases approx 1500-2000/yr but low information content since largely anticipated

clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: most of the informative subset survives

survivorship.price_side: moderate - issuers/payers skew healthier and larger (less severe bias) but the cut/omission leg specifically skews toward firms that go on to underperform or delist

families.quant_v7_contamination: PARTIALLY USED - the fundamentals family (RESEARCH_LEDGER row 19) already tested a monthly net-share-issuance-ratio signal on the same underlying issuance data (all negative). OSAP's ShareIss1Y/ShareIss5Y and DivOmit predictors remain 2015+ survivors in the project's own edge-graveyard study (2015+ Sharpe 0.82-0.88 and 0.82 respectively) - an encouraging but not fully independent prior. A discrete declaration-date event study is a genuinely different construction from the monthly ratio already tested, but shares the same underlying economic story, which is why this ranks 3rd rather than 1st despite strong power and mechanism.
families.implementation_realism: HIGH - same EDGAR plumbing as family 1
families.caveat: if the director weights criterion 7 (independence from prior research) more heavily than its listed lowest-priority position, IPO lockups (rank 4) would be the cleaner #3 pick

families.name: IPO lockup expirations (~180 days after pricing, sometimes staged 25/50/75% releases)

mechanism.class: pre-scheduled supply shock as insiders become free to sell
literature: Field & Hanka (2001): 3-day CAR approx -1.5% and a permanent approx 40% volume increase at expiry
Bradley, Jordan, Roten & Yi (2001); Ofek & Richardson (2000, dot-com vintage): effect well known to the Street since the late 1990s, likely partially arbitraged since

source.primary: IPO prospectus (S-1/424B4) lockup language on SEC EDGAR - the date is fixed and public at pricing

timing.exact_field: lockup date stated in the prospectus
timing.timezone: n/a - date known in advance, no intraday precision needed
timing.next_tradable_execution: the trading session the lockup lifts (typically 12:01am after N days)

counts.events_per_year: approx 150-400 at current US IPO volume (roughly 150-300 IPOs/yr, some staged) - the smallest count among the top group, at the low end of the hundreds target
counts.history_available: EDGAR era (1994+); modern IPO volume is well below the 1999-2021 peaks

clustering.profile: low-moderate - echoes the IPO calendar's own seasonal clustering (spring/fall windows)
clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: most of the raw count survives

survivorship.event_side: unbiased - dates are public at pricing
survivorship.price_side: BEST IN CLASS - newly IPO'd names are almost tautologically present in current free price feeds at event time; multi-year post-IPO studies still want delisted-inclusive coverage since some IPOs fail within 1-2 years

families.quant_v7_contamination: GENUINELY NEW - zero hits anywhere in research/ or reports/
families.implementation_realism: HIGH - pure EDGAR text/date extraction, no real-time feed needed since dates are known in advance
families.note: strongest survivorship/PIT/novelty profile of any family; held back only by a raw count at the low end of the hundreds target

families.name: Monthly options-expiration cross-section: single-stock OI-based pinning / unwinding

mechanism.class: dealer gamma-hedging pins the underlying near high-open-interest strikes into expiration; unwinds as dealers roll hedges after
literature: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (2005): statistically significant pinning documented

source.is_free: yes for the OCC-wide aggregate report (confirmed); per-symbol access plausible via a query tool at marketdata.theocc.com but UNCONFIRMED beyond a structured HTTP 400 (endpoint exists, parameters not yet solved)
source.probe_evidence: data/event_scout/occ_daily_open_interest.txt - free CSV, e.g. 09/24/2026 equity calls 345,176,512 / puts 254,102,209 (OCC-wide totals only, not per-underlying)

timing.exact_field: OI computed once daily after the close, available at the start of the next session; expiration = 3rd Friday of the month at the close
timing.next_tradable_execution: same/next session, concentrated in the final session(s) before expiration

counts.events_per_year: 12 monthly expirations/yr x hundreds of optionable underlyings with meaningful OI = thousands of underlying-expiration cells/yr, though many names have negligible OI and should be filtered, shrinking the effective universe
counts.history_available: OCC aggregate history exists; this session only pulled September 2026; deeper per-symbol history depth is unconfirmed

clustering.profile: high within a given expiration Friday (market-wide gamma effects move together); moderate across the 12 dates/yr
clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: ~12 largely independent calendar dates/yr, each with a rich but correlated cross-section

survivorship.price_side: moderate - optionable names skew larger/still-listed so less severe than broad equity, but not delisted-inclusive

families.quant_v7_contamination: PARTIALLY explored at the INDEX level only - index_option_breadth (SPY/QQQ/IWM volume breadth) FAILED and is locked/SPENT, but that used trade-print volume breadth on 3 names, not per-name OI-based pinning across hundreds of stocks. The explicit avoid-list item is 'OpEx SPY put writing', a different index-level options-selling structure. Single-name OI-based pinning is GENUINELY NEW.
families.implementation_realism: MEDIUM - aggregate OI confirmed free; per-symbol OI needs a follow-up feasibility check before committing
families.note: directly answers the mandate's instruction to check CBOE/OCC free data since the LSE has no open interest; gated on confirming per-symbol OCC access

families.name: Crypto perpetual-future funding-rate settlements (8-hourly, cross-sectional)

mechanism.class: positioning-crowding - extreme funding reflects one-sided leveraged demand that tends to mean-revert
literature: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2022): crypto basis/funding predictability - evidence base thinner and newer than equity-event literature

source.primary: Binance public REST API (also OKX, Bybit, dYdX)
source.probe_evidence: data/event_scout/binance_funding_btcusdt.json - 5 consecutive BTCUSDT settlements exactly 28800s (8h) apart; data/event_scout/binance_exchangeinfo.json - 570 TRADING USDT-margined perpetuals live on Binance alone

timing.next_tradable_execution: continuous - perpetuals trade every second; the funding print itself is a payment, not a trade

counts.events_per_year: 570 perpetuals x 3 settlements/day x 365 = approx 624,000 coin-settlements/yr on Binance alone; approx 55,000-110,000/yr restricted to the liquid top 50-100 coins - the largest raw count of any candidate
counts.history_available: Binance USDM perpetuals launched 2019-2020; per-symbol depth varies

clustering.profile: VERY HIGH - every coin settles at the same 3 clock-times/day, so daily cross-sections are not independent draws of the calendar
clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: ~3 independent clock-times/day (~1095/yr) is the real time-series unit; cross-sectional independence WITHIN a settlement is good since each coin's funding is largely idiosyncratic

survivorship.price_side: SEVERE - exchanges delist failed/illiquid perpetuals routinely; no free delisted-inclusive crypto history exists comparable to Sharadar's equity coverage

families.quant_v7_contamination: GENUINELY NEW mechanism (funding-rate crowding) and universe (500+ coins), though the BTC/ETH trend family (SPENT) already touched the crypto asset class broadly. Likely overlaps the parallel Binance-crypto data workload assigned to another agent - route data-pull ownership before duplicating effort.
families.implementation_realism: HIGH - trivial, well-documented free API, confirmed working this session
families.note: huge headline count but severe clustering and crypto survivorship problems keep it out of the top 3

families.name: Index reconstitution effective dates: Russell 1000/2000/3000 (semi-annual from Dec 2026), S&P 400/500/600 (quarterly + ad hoc), MSCI (quarterly)

mechanism.class: forced, non-informational passive-fund trading at a publicly pre-announced instant
literature: Chen, Noronha & Singal (2004); Petajisto (2011, 'The Index Premium and Its Hidden Cost for Index Funds'): a real but shrinking index-premium/hidden-cost effect

quant_v7's OWN edge-graveyard catalogue (reports/edge_graveyard/REPORT.md) independently lists the classic 'S&P inclusion pop' as a DEAD published effect, consistent with heavy front-running by index-arb desks since the late 1990s

source.primary: FTSE Russell press releases/PDFs; S&P DJI press releases; MSCI quarterly index review results
source.verified_in_session: via web search - confirmed the official June 26 2026 Russell effective-date PDF and the new Dec-2026 semi-annual reconstitution date (first ever December Russell reconstitution)

timing.next_tradable_execution: passive funds execute at/near the announced close, so any edge is in the announcement-to-effective run-up or post-effective reversal, not intraday timing

counts.events_per_year: Russell June alone moves 300-600+ constituent changes on ONE day; the new Dec 2026 date roughly doubles this; S&P 400/500/600 combined approx 150-250 changes/yr on ~4 dates each; MSCI adds more on its own quarterly dates - combined hundreds to over a thousand NAME-changes/yr
counts.history_available: Russell since 1979 (annual, now transitioning to semi-annual); S&P and MSCI for decades

clustering.profile: EXTREME - the overwhelming majority of a year's changes land on approx 6-10 distinct calendar dates total across all three families, even though the stock-count per date is large
clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: approx 6-10 independent trial DATES per year - too few to compute a meaningful annualized Sharpe under quant_v7's own sqrt(T)-scaled dev gate, since T counts calendar years of trial time, not event count

survivorship.event_side: unbiased - membership lists are public and known in advance
survivorship.price_side: moderate - adds are usually large/liquid; deletes are often small/illiquid and sometimes later delisted

families.quant_v7_contamination: GENUINELY NEW as an executed trial (flagged in research/EDGE_GRAVEYARD_PLAN.md Phase 3-A3 but never run), though the headline announcement-pop mechanism is literature-dead per the project's own prior work - partial, literature-level contamination rather than project-level
families.implementation_realism: MEDIUM - official sources are free but require manual PDF/press-release parsing rather than a structured bulk API; no free historical membership-change feed was confirmed
families.note: the mandate explicitly warns to mind clustering and post-publication decay for this family; both concerns are confirmed serious here. The one genuinely fresh sub-opportunity is the brand-new Dec-2026 Russell date, unstudied because it has never happened before.

families.name: Reg SHO threshold-securities-list additions (persistent settlement fails forcing a Rule 203(b)(3) buy-in)

mechanism.class: forced close-out buying after 13 consecutive settlement days of fails-to-deliver
literature: Boulton & Braga-Alves (2010); Fotak, Raman & Yadav (Reg SHO pilot studies)

source.probe_evidence: data/event_scout/nasdaq_regsho_threshold_today.txt - 200 OK, pipe-delimited, ~20+ names on 2026-09-24, mostly small-cap (S) and leveraged/inverse ETPs (G)

timing.exact_field: daily list date; the ADDITION (a symbol newly appearing vs. the prior day's list) is the tradable event
timing.timezone: trading-day granularity; list published before the next session's open

counts.events_per_year: the list is short each day; unique ADDITION events likely number in the low-to-mid hundreds/yr, smaller than hoped and concentrated in illiquid names
counts.history_available: Nasdaq/NYSE lists published daily for years; FINRA/SEC fails-to-deliver data back to 2004 (complete from 2008-09-16)

clustering.profile: low (idiosyncratic per name) but the affected universe is itself a bad-liquidity pool
clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: most of the count survives as independent trials but the pool is small

survivorship.price_side: HIGH RISK - threshold names are disproportionately distressed/small/hard-to-borrow; many later delist or go to zero, the worst survivorship profile among the SEC/exchange-filing-based candidates

families.quant_v7_contamination: GENUINELY NEW as a discrete ADDITION-event design (data_scout catalogued raw FTD levels as a data source, never as a threshold-list event). Overlaps the parallel public-market-data agent's FINRA short-volume/short-interest territory at the data-source level - event DESIGN only was evaluated here.
families.implementation_realism: HIGH - confirmed free and simple to poll daily

families.name: Stock splits (forward) and reverse splits (announcement date)

mechanism.class: forward-split signalling (managerial confidence / lower tick size) vs. reverse-split going-concern/compliance signal
literature: Ikenberry, Rankine & Stice (1996): forward-split announcement drift approx +7-9% over the following year, a 1990s-vintage finding likely heavily arbitraged/decayed since; reverse-split literature is thinner and more recent (post-2022 Nasdaq $1 minimum-bid-price compliance wave)

source.primary: SEC EDGAR 8-K Item 3.03/5.03 + press release; Sharadar ACTIONS table

timing.next_tradable_execution: next session open/close depending on filing time

counts.events_per_year: forward splits among liquid names are now rare (approx 20-50/yr); reverse splits have surged since 2022 to plausibly several hundred/yr but concentrated almost entirely in distressed micro/small-cap and OTC names

survivorship.price_side: SEVERE for the reverse-split leg specifically - reverse splits are disproportionately a precursor to delisting, i.e. the event-side population overlaps almost exactly with the population free price feeds are worst at covering going forward

families.quant_v7_contamination: GENUINELY NEW as an event study in this project
families.implementation_realism: HIGH - same EDGAR plumbing as family 1

families.name: Crypto token-unlock vesting cliffs

literature: mirrors the IPO-lockup logic; rigorous academic literature is thin-to-nonexistent for crypto unlocks specifically

source.is_free: NO confirmed free structured/bulk API (web calendars only; API tiers appear paid); ground truth is on-chain vesting-contract data, free but requires per-project engineering to parse

timing.exact_field: scheduled unlock date, often to the UTC day or specific block

counts.events_per_year: hundreds of tokens have periodic (often monthly) unlock cliffs - plausibly hundreds to low-thousands of unlock events/yr in aggregate
counts.history_available: vesting schedules set at token generation; historical depth varies enormously by project and is largely undocumented centrally

clustering.effective_independent_trials_per_year: most of the raw count IF the data were reliably free
